ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: the game version banner
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: This is the version line RimWorld prints at startup so the log records exactly which build you are on. It is purely informational.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: the command-line arguments line
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: RimWorld records the launch options it was started with (for example a custom save-data folder set by a mod manager or launcher). It is a normal startup note, not a problem.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: save-data folder was redirected
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: You launched with a custom save-data folder, so RimWorld is reading and writing its configs and saves there instead of the default location. A mod manager, a launcher, or a test tool does this on purpose. Nothing is wrong.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: the active mod list for a new game
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: When you start a new game, RimWorld lists the mods that are loaded so the log has a record of them. The packageIds after it are just that list; none of them are being blamed for anything.

ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.label: the active mod list for a loaded save
ModernDevTools.KnownIssueDef.description: When you load a save, RimWorld lists the mods it is loading with so the log has a record of them. The packageIds after it are just that list; none of them are being blamed for anything.
